params.body:
# Deploy: warm the caches instead of letting the first dealer wait

## Why

On the morning of 2026-09-14 the first request to `/stocklist` after a deploy on staging took
over twenty seconds and ended in a Cloudflare 504. A refresh right after was instant. That is a
cold start: the facet lists, the counts per category group and per manufacturer and the two
histograms behind the stocklist are group-by queries over the whole stocklist population, cached
for fifteen minutes in `StocklistBrowser` and `OwnStockList`. When the cache is empty, ONE
visitor builds all of them, and after the cutover that visitor is a dealer.

Behaviour is unchanged; nothing a user sees moves. This adds a command, a scheduled run and two
lines of deploy documentation.

## What the cold start consists of

Measured locally with `stocklist:warm` itself (it reports per cache key), on MariaDB 12 with a
synthetic set of 20,000 stocklist vehicles, 25 dealers, 3 category groups, 1 locale. The
boundaries are the cache's own `CacheMissed` and `KeyWritten` events, so each row is that key's
own build and nothing else; `(uncached work)` is everything outside a miss/write pair.

Cold cache, 1424 ms total:

| cache key | ms | queries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(uncached work)` (x8) | 352 | 60 |
| `ownstock_filterlists_*` (x25) | 566 | 75 |
| `sl_group_total_*` (x3) | 244 | 9 |
| `sl_man_counts_*` (x3) | 68 | 3 |
| `sl_group_counts` | 50 | 1 |
| `sl_categories_*` (x3) | 33 | 3 |
| `sl_km_histo` | 30 | 2 |
| `sl_year_histo` | 19 | 1 |
| `ownstock_portalopts_*` (x25) | 12 | 25 |
| `sl_manufacturers`, `sl_fuel`, `sl_colors`, `sl_paint`, `sl_transmission`, `sl_options`, `sl_countries`, `sl_dealers_*`, `sl_dealer_groups`, `sl_mileage_max`, `sl_bodystyles_*` | 1 to 6 each | 1 to 3 each |

The same run with the cache already warm: 318 ms, 87 queries, all of it in `(uncached work)`.

Reading that: the cacheable part is about 1060 ms of the 1424, spread over 77 keys. A single
visitor does not pay all of it (they pay the shared keys plus their own category group and their
own dealer: roughly 230 ms here), but a deploy empties all 77 at once, and a deploy also empties
the InnoDB buffer pool's usefulness for these scans on a restarted box. Staging's real
population is a multiple of this set and its search joins the photo tables, which is how 230 ms
becomes twenty seconds there. The shape is what transfers, not the milliseconds: run
`php artisan stocklist:warm --queries` on staging for its own numbers.

Two findings worth naming, neither fixed here:

- **The dominant query shape is the same one, four times.** `count(distinct vehicles.id)` over
  `vehicles` joined to `vehicle_categories` and `dealers`, filtered on
  `available_on_stocklist = 1 AND sold = 0 AND for_export = 0 AND is_accident_vehicle = 0 AND
  dealers.module_2 = 1 AND dealers.is_demo_user = 0`, grouped by category group
  (`sl_group_counts`), by manufacturer (`sl_man_counts_*`), by construction year
  (`sl_year_histo`) and by mileage bucket (`sl_km_histo`). The only index on `vehicles` that
  touches this is `search_index (available_on_stocklist, available_on_stocklist_date)`; `sold`,
  `for_export` and `is_accident_vehicle` are not in any index. A composite index over those four
  columns is the obvious candidate, but it is not a one-liner you add blind: it wants an EXPLAIN
  on the real table and a look at what else writes to `vehicles`. Separate PR, with the numbers
  from staging.
- **`(uncached work)` is 304 ms warm and no amount of warming touches it.** That is the live
  `extendedSearch` per group plus the thirteen card relations eager-loaded per page. Every
  visitor pays that on every visit. It is the next thing to look at after this PR, and the
  command now measures it for you.

Aside, noticed while writing the test: `phpunit.xml` sets `CACHE_STORE=array`, but
`config/cache.php` reads `CACHE_DRIVER`, so the suite actually runs on the file cache and cached
values survive between tests and between runs. Not touched here (changing the test cache driver
for the whole suite is its own change); the new test forgets its keys explicitly so it cannot
pass on a leftover.

## What the command warms

`php artisan stocklist:warm` (`app/Console/Commands/WarmCaches.php`), parts selectable with
`--only=framework,stocklist,ownstock,bidding`:

- **stocklist**: one render of `StocklistBrowser` per category group per locale in use, with
  `readyToLoad` on so the group total and the search are covered too (the list arrives in a
  second round trip and a visitor waits for that one just as long). Fills `sl_manufacturers`,
  `sl_transmission`, `sl_fuel`, `sl_colors`, `sl_paint`, `sl_mileage_max`, `sl_options`,
  `sl_dealer_groups`, `sl_countries`, `sl_postal_ranges`, `sl_dealers_0`, `sl_group_counts`,
  `sl_year_histo`, `sl_km_histo`, and per group `sl_man_counts_*`, `sl_categories_*`,
  `sl_group_total_*`, `sl_bodystyles_*_<locale>`.
- **ownstock**: one render of `OwnStockList` per dealer (`--dealers=n` caps it). Fills
  `ownstock_filter_options` once and `ownstock_filterlists_<dealer>` plus
  `ownstock_portalopts_<dealer>` per dealer.
- **bidding**: nothing to warm, and it says so. `BiddingOfferBrowser` caches nothing; its query
  runs live on every render. A part that is silently absent reads as a part that was forgotten.
- **framework**: reports whether the config, route, event and view caches are present. It does
  not build them — the deploy does, with `php artisan optimize` (confirmed by 2f31a4b and
  `RouteCacheTest`) — and rebuilding them on a live box means clearing them first, so every
  request in between recompiles. `--framework` builds a missing one for a hand-set box.

Two design points, both about not lying:

1. **It warms by rendering the components, not by repeating their queries.** A warmer holding its
   own copy of the cache keys starts filling keys nobody reads the moment one is renamed, and it
   does that silently: the page stays slow and the command keeps reporting success. Rendering is
   the only way the keys cannot drift. Nothing is written to the database and no view is rendered
   to HTML.
2. **It verifies and it measures.** After warming it checks the keys it claims against the cache
   and names any that are missing (that list is a check, never the builder, so a rename shows up
   as "missing" instead of disappearing). Per key it reports milliseconds, queries and, with
   `--queries`, the slowest query.

Safe to run twice (a warm key is a hit) and safe on an empty database: with no dealer user to
warm for it says so and exits 0.

## Schedule

`routes/console.php`:

```php
Schedule::command('stocklist:warm --only=stocklist,ownstock --refresh')
    ->everyTenMinutes()
    ->withoutOverlapping(10);
```

Ten minutes, under the fifteen-minute TTL of every key it fills. `--refresh` drops the keys
before rebuilding them, and that flag is the whole point: `remember()` does NOT renew a key that
is still alive, so without it the run at t=10 is a hit, the key still dies at t=15, and the gap
until t=20 is exactly the cold start being removed here. The cost is a window of about a second
in which a request could rebuild the same key itself; that is why it is not the default (a deploy
warms an empty cache and has nothing to forget).

Only the data caches are scheduled. The framework caches have no TTL, are invalidated by the
deploy and are excluded on purpose.

## Cutover line

`CUTOVER.md` section 2, next to the migrations:

> **In het Forge-deployscript, meteen NA `php artisan migrate --force` (en na `optimize`):
> `php8.5 artisan stocklist:warm`.**

and a new section 5c with the reasoning, the framework-cache split, the schedule and how to check
it afterwards. Also corrected in the same file: the "optioneel na go-live" item saying
`route:cache` could not be switched on yet is stale since 2026-09-11 (`merchant.update` was the
duplicate, fixed in 2f31a4b, and the deploy runs `optimize`). `README.md` gains the command in its
list.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='Warm|Stocklist|SmokeTest|ClassReferencesResolve|Schedule'`: 154
  tests, 272 assertions, no failures. Own MySQL database, loaded from
  `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations as CI does, dropped
  afterwards.
- `tests/Feature/WarmCachesTest.php`: runs on an empty database (exit 0, says there is nothing to
  warm), fills the keys it claims after explicitly forgetting them first, is safe to run twice,
  and reports the framework caches without building them.
- Ran by hand cold, warm and with `--refresh` against a 20,000-vehicle set; the tables above are
  those runs.
- Not touched: any `.env`.
